title: Fake followers, audience ownership and algorithm changes

sections.skill: Avoid fake followers and reduce dependence on one platform

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: Why are fake followers harmful?

choices.text: They buy more than real followers
They inflate counts but never buy

questions.correct_answer: They inflate counts but never buy
questions.intro: Big numbers can mislead. FAKE FOLLOWERS (bought or bot accounts) inflate counts but never buy, and can hurt how a platform shows your posts. AUDIENCE OWNERSHIP: on social platforms, the platform controls who sees your posts and can change its rules or ALGORITHM (the system that decides what people see) at any time, or suspend accounts. An email list or customer list that people joined with permission is closer to an audience you control. Build some of both, and never rely on a single platform.

sections.skill: Renting a stall versus owning a address book

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: A social platform is like what?

choices.text: Your own building on your own land
A rented stall in someone else's market

questions.correct_answer: A rented stall in someone else's market
questions.intro: Selling on a social platform is like renting a stall in someone else's market. The market owner decides where your stall goes, how many people walk past, and whether you can stay. Your email list is like your own address book of customers who asked to hear from you. If the market closes or moves you to a corner, you can still write to your address book.
